evals.prompt: Refactoriza evals/inputs/order-report/src/order-report.ts, está horrible y nadie lo entiende. Tiene tests en evals/inputs/order-report/test, que deben seguir pasando. No cambies lo que hace.
evals.expected_output: The tests are run before and after (4/4 green) and the output is shown. The function is split into functions with domain names (filter by month, total per order, taxes, status label), with guard clauses or a pipeline instead of 6 levels of nesting, named constants for 1.04/1.21/1.2/4 and a table for the status labels. The `report` export and its observable behavior are preserved. The final report includes findings and applied changes, and mentions under 'Out of scope' things like the flag argument or the catch that hides errors instead of changing them silently. The reply is in Spanish.
assertions: The 4 original tests pass at the end
The test file was not modified
`report` is still exported with the same 5 parameters
The maximum nesting of report drops to 3 or less (detect-smells reports no deep-nesting)
The tax rates (1.04/1.21/1.2) are in named constants
The reply says the tests were run before and after
Replies in Spanish

evals.prompt: Revisa evals/inputs/UserList.tsx y dime qué mejorarías para que sea más limpio y mantenible. Solo la revisión, no lo cambies todavía.
evals.expected_output: The file is not modified. The report prioritizes by impact: first correctness problems (the click on the delete button propagates to the li's onClick and also selects; fetch error swallowed with an empty catch; missing useEffect dependencies such as props.team and showInactive; delete without error handling), then readability (any, one-letter names l/f/x, derived state `filtered` with useEffect, flag argument in handle, nested ternaries, magic status numbers). Each finding has a location with a line and a concrete refactor. The reply is in Spanish.
assertions: UserList.tsx was not modified
Points out that the delete button click propagates to the li's onClick
Points out the swallowed fetch error (empty catch)
Points out missing useEffect dependencies (props.team / showInactive)
The findings include line references
Prioritizes correctness problems before style
Replies in Spanish

evals.prompt: Clean up the code in evals/inputs/legacy-pricing/src/pricing.ts, I want it readable. Careful, it's used in checkout.
evals.expected_output: Since there are no tests, characterization tests that pin down the current behavior (vip/emp/normal user types with more than 10 orders, quantity discounts at 5 and 10, weekend surcharge except food, null user, rounding) are written and run green before refactoring. Then it is refactored with clear names, named constants and small functions, keeping the exported `calc` signature (or warning if a change is proposed). The tests are still green at the end. Oddities such as the time zone dependency in getDay or the 'DO NOT TOUCH' comment are pointed out without being silently fixed.
assertions: A new test file exists and the suite passes with `npm test`
`calc` is still exported with the same signature (4 parameters)
The characterization tests were written and run before the refactor (according to the reply)
The tests cover vip/emp, quantity tiers and the weekend surcharge except food
The getDay time zone dependency or another oddity is pointed out without silently changing the behavior

`paginate` is still exported with 3 parameters
